title: Fun Quiz: TCR, MHC and Immunoglobulins

questions.question: What is the usual structural description of a T-cell receptor?
options: A heterodimer made of alpha-beta or gamma-delta chains
A pentamer made of five identical heavy chains
A single secreted light chain
A homodimer found only in serum
questions.answer: A heterodimer made of alpha-beta or gamma-delta chains
questions.explanation: A T-cell receptor is a heterodimer. Its two different chains are usually alpha and beta, or gamma and delta. Each chain contains variable and constant regions.
questions.similar_question: Which pair can form the two chains of a T-cell receptor?

questions.question: How do T cells normally recognize antigen?
options: As processed peptide presented by MHC on a cell surface
As free soluble antigen in blood
Only after the antigen binds an antibody
By secreting T-cell receptors into plasma
questions.answer: As processed peptide presented by MHC on a cell surface
questions.explanation: T cells do not normally recognize free antigen. Their receptors recognize processed peptide together with an MHC molecule on a cell membrane, a principle called MHC restriction.
questions.similar_question: Which statement best demonstrates MHC restriction?
similar_options: A TCR responds to a peptide only when it is displayed by an appropriate MHC molecule
An antibody binds a soluble toxin
A mast cell releases histamine after IgE cross-linking
questions.similar_correct_answer: A TCR responds to a peptide only when it is displayed by an appropriate MHC molecule

questions.question: Which pairing is correct for the MHC class I pathway?
options: Endogenous peptide - MHC I - CD8 T cell
Exogenous peptide - MHC I - CD4 T cell
Endogenous peptide - MHC II - CD8 T cell
Free antigen - MHC I - B cell
questions.answer: Endogenous peptide - MHC I - CD8 T cell
questions.explanation: MHC class I molecules are expressed on nearly all nucleated cells and usually present peptides generated within the cell. These complexes are recognized by CD8 cytotoxic T cells.
questions.similar_question: A virus-infected nucleated cell displays a viral peptide to a cytotoxic T cell. Which molecule most likely presents it?

questions.question: Which pairing is correct for the MHC class II pathway?
options: Exogenous peptide - antigen-presenting cell - CD4 T cell
Endogenous peptide - every red blood cell - CD8 T cell
Free antigen - plasma cell - CD8 T cell
Cytosolic peptide - mast cell - B cell
questions.answer: Exogenous peptide - antigen-presenting cell - CD4 T cell
questions.explanation: MHC class II is mainly expressed by professional antigen-presenting cells such as dendritic cells, macrophages and B cells. It presents peptides derived from material taken up from outside the cell to CD4 helper T cells.
questions.similar_question: Which cell is a professional antigen-presenting cell that can display peptide on MHC class II?

questions.question: What is the main role of TAP during endogenous antigen processing?
options: Transport peptides from the cytosol into the endoplasmic reticulum
Degrade invariant chain into CLIP
Carry MHC class II from lysosomes to the nucleus
Cross-link IgE on mast cells
questions.answer: Transport peptides from the cytosol into the endoplasmic reticulum
questions.explanation: TAP is an ATP-dependent heterodimeric transporter associated with antigen processing. It moves proteasome-generated peptides into the ER, where suitable peptides can bind assembling MHC class I molecules.
questions.similar_question: Where do proteasome-generated peptides go to bind newly assembled MHC class I molecules?

questions.question: What prevents peptides from binding prematurely to the MHC class II groove in the endoplasmic reticulum?
options: Invariant chain
TAP
Perforin
IgM J chain
questions.explanation: Invariant chain, also called Ii or CD74, occupies the MHC class II peptide-binding groove during assembly. It is later degraded to CLIP, which is exchanged for antigenic peptide with help from HLA-DM.
questions.similar_question: Which molecule promotes replacement of CLIP with an antigenic peptide in an endosomal compartment?

questions.question: Which mechanism can a CD8 cytotoxic T cell use to kill an infected target cell?
options: Release perforin and granzymes to trigger apoptosis
Secrete pentameric IgM
Produce invariant chain
Convert CLIP into TAP
questions.answer: Release perforin and granzymes to trigger apoptosis
questions.explanation: Cytotoxic T cells kill target cells by inducing apoptosis. They can release perforin, which helps granzymes enter the target, or engage the Fas death receptor through Fas ligand.
questions.similar_question: Which receptor-ligand pair can activate an apoptotic death pathway in a cytotoxic T-cell target?

questions.question: Which immunoglobulin is the most abundant antibody class in serum?
options: IgG
IgM
IgA
IgE
questions.explanation: IgG accounts for about 80% of serum immunoglobulin. Important IgG activities include neutralization, opsonization, complement activation by some subclasses and placental transfer.
questions.similar_question: Which antibody class is especially important for protecting a fetus and newborn through placental transfer?

questions.question: Which description best fits secreted IgM?
options: A pentamer that appears early in a primary immune response
A monomer that is the main antibody in tears
A dimer that crosses the placenta
A rare antibody bound mainly to mast cells
questions.answer: A pentamer that appears early in a primary immune response
questions.explanation: Secreted IgM is pentameric, has high valence and is the first major antibody produced during a primary immune response. Its arrangement also makes it highly effective at activating complement.
questions.similar_question: Which immunoglobulin is generally more efficient than IgG at activating complement?

questions.question: Which immunoglobulin predominates in secretions such as milk, saliva, tears and mucus?
options: IgA
IgG
IgD
IgE
questions.explanation: IgA provides localized protection at mucosal surfaces and is the predominant immunoglobulin in many secretions. Secretory IgA commonly contains a J chain and secretory component acquired during epithelial transport.
questions.similar_question: Which process carries polymeric IgA across an epithelial cell into a secretion?

questions.question: IgE bound to mast cells is most directly associated with which event?
options: Immediate hypersensitivity and histamine release
Placental antibody transfer
MHC class I peptide loading
Expression of IgD on naive B cells
questions.explanation: IgE binds high-affinity Fc epsilon receptors on mast cells and basophils. Cross-linking of cell-bound IgE by allergen triggers degranulation and release of mediators such as histamine.
questions.similar_question: Cross-linking which mast-cell-bound antibody class can contribute to anaphylaxis?

questions.question: During immunoglobulin class switching, what changes?
options: The heavy-chain constant region changes while antigen specificity is retained
The light-chain variable region is replaced and specificity is lost
The entire V(D)J region is deleted
The B cell changes into a T cell
questions.answer: The heavy-chain constant region changes while antigen specificity is retained
questions.explanation: Class-switch recombination replaces the heavy-chain constant region, allowing the antibody to gain a different effector class such as IgG, IgA or IgE. The rearranged variable region is preserved, so antigen specificity does not change.
questions.similar_question: A B-cell clone switches from IgM to IgG. What should remain the same?
similar_options: Its secretory location in every tissue
Its requirement to express only IgM

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes V(D)J recombination from class-switch recombination?
options: V(D)J recombination requires RAG proteins, whereas class switching does not
Class switching creates the first variable region in a pro-B cell
V(D)J recombination occurs only after repeated antigen exposure
Both processes always change antigen specificity
questions.answer: V(D)J recombination requires RAG proteins, whereas class switching does not
questions.explanation: V(D)J recombination builds the variable-region exon during antigen-independent B-cell development and requires RAG1/RAG2. Class-switch recombination occurs after activation, targets switch regions and changes the heavy-chain constant region without requiring RAG proteins.
questions.similar_question: Where does V(D)J recombination normally occur as part of antigen-independent B-cell development?

questions.question: What is the difference between antibody affinity and avidity?
options: Affinity is one binding-site interaction; avidity is the combined strength of multiple interactions
Affinity applies only to IgM; avidity applies only to IgG
Affinity measures antibody concentration; avidity measures complement concentration
They are two names for exactly the same measurement
questions.answer: Affinity is one binding-site interaction; avidity is the combined strength of multiple interactions
questions.explanation: Affinity describes the strength between one antigen-binding site and one ligand or epitope. Avidity describes the overall strength produced when a multivalent antibody makes multiple simultaneous contacts with a multivalent antigen.
questions.similar_question: A pentameric IgM binds through several sites at once. Which term best describes the total strength of all those contacts?
